    Scalar automorphisms act trivially on module classes #

    Lemma 4.13, first step: "A weight scales morphism lines and thus defines an automorphism of L. These automorphisms act on the indecomposable module classes with any fixed finite support […]. Their permutation image is finite, abelian and divisible, hence trivial. Every scalar automorphism consequently fixes each V_X̃ up to isomorphism."

    For a finite set of objects s of the graded covering category, a weight d defines the automorphism σ_d of the covering algebra cov D s scaling the (p, q)-entry by d(s p, s q) (scaleEquiv). By divisibility of weights (Lemma 4.11(2)) σ_d = σ_e^N for the N of twist_pow_iso, so σ_d fixes every finite-dimensional indecomposable class (weight_twist_iso).

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
